checks.statement: Use the contained search style as the recommended style; it has a persistent filled container. The divided style is baseline and lacks the latest visual style, motion, and trailing-icon flexibility.
checks.condition: When selecting or implementing an M3 Expressive search style.

sourceHistory.summary: Expressive update recommends contained styling and describes divided style as baseline.

implementation.notes: Choosing which design-system style to recommend is product/design-system policy; the baseline exposes both variants but does not select a product recommendation.

checks.statement: In M3 Expressive, the search bar grows wider when focused.
checks.condition: When using M3 Expressive search.

sourceHistory.summary: Expressive update specifies search-bar width growth on focus.

evidence.result: Opening focused search expands the view from the closed bar to a results surface and transitions its width/position; contained and divided styles both share this open-state layout.

checks.statement: M3 search bars use rounded shapes and tonal surface, with lower elevation and no default shadow; use the M3 color mappings, which support dynamic color.
checks.condition: When applying M3 baseline search styling or documenting its difference from M2.

sourceHistory.summary: M2 comparison describes M3 color, elevation, shape, and tonal-surface changes.

evidence.result: The closed surface has no shadow by default; the bar uses token-backed container, shape, and surface color variables.

checks.statement: The Search variant is available in both M3 and M3 Expressive.
checks.condition: When selecting the documented search variant for either design system version.

sourceHistory.summary: Variants table marks Search available in M3 and M3 Expressive.

implementation.notes: This web baseline implements one Material token/variant model and does not select between separately versioned M3 and Expressive products.

checks.statement: Choose contained or divided search styling. Contained uses a filled container to distinguish the bar from suggestions or results; divided uses a divider and is the baseline style without the latest expressive visuals, motion, or flexibility.
checks.condition: When choosing the visual style of a search experience.

sourceHistory.summary: Style section defines contained and divided configurations and their distinction.

evidence.result: The preview exposes baseline/divided and contained choices; CSS gives baseline its divider and contained its filled-bar treatment.

checks.statement: Use either docked or full-screen layout for the suggestions or results list beneath the search bar.
checks.condition: When choosing a focused-search results layout.

sourceHistory.summary: Layout section identifies docked and full-screen configurations.

evidence.result: SearchLayout preserves docked/full-screen choices (adaptive currently resolves to docked); CSS has separate docked and full-screen open-state rules.

checks.statement: Provide a search bar and a suggestions/results container; the container is empty by default and uses the list component for content. In divided style, separate the bar and results with a divider.
checks.condition: When structuring the search component.

sourceHistory.summary: Anatomy prose specifies the bar, empty list container, list component, and divided-style divider.

evidence.result: The rendered search view includes a search bar and results container; results use the list component, and baseline style adds a top divider.

checks.statement: Represent the search bar's enabled, hovered, focused, and pressed (ripple) states.
checks.condition: For the search bar interaction states shown in the component specification.

sourceHistory.summary: Search bar state list names enabled, hovered, focused, and pressed states.

evidence.result: Code defines focus-visible and pressed styling, but this evidence does not establish the required hover state or that all enabled-state appearance matches the guidance.

implementation.notes: No focused browser/style inspection was run for the state set.

checks.statement: Represent enabled, hovered, focused, and pressed (ripple) states for suggestion and result items.
checks.condition: For interactive search suggestion and result items.

sourceHistory.summary: Suggestions and results state list names enabled, hovered, focused, and pressed states.

evidence.result: Each suggestion/result is a list-item button, so the result controls use the shared list-item interaction states rather than a custom search-only state layer.

checks.statement: Use search for products with many items to manage, such as files or messages.
checks.condition: When deciding whether a product or view needs search.

sourceHistory.summary: Usage recommends search for products with many items to manage.

implementation.notes: Whether a product collection is large enough to need search is a product-level choice, not established by the reusable search implementation.

checks.statement: Choose the entry point by the product need: use a search bar for content in a specific view, a persistent search app bar integrated into the app bar for primary global search, and a search icon button when search is secondary or not the main focus.
checks.condition: When choosing where search is exposed in a product.

sourceHistory.summary: Guidelines map search bar, search app bar, and icon button to view-scoped, global, and secondary search.

implementation.notes: Choosing a local bar, persistent app-bar search, or secondary icon entry point is product navigation architecture; this component implements the search experience after entry.

checks.statement: On focus, suggestions may appear before text entry; suggestions or results may update while typing or after a search is executed. Individual focused elements keep their own interaction states.
checks.condition: When a search entry point opens focused search.

sourceHistory.summary: Focused-search section describes suggestion/result timing and independent interaction states.

evidence.result: Opening search filters and announces suggestions; typing filters results and updates the heading to quick results/results while retaining per-item list controls.

checks.statement: Use the list component for suggestions and results; consider adding related leading icons, category labels, avatars or other high-priority items, and filter chips to provide variety and context.
checks.condition: When presenting search suggestions or results.

sourceHistory.summary: Guidance describes list-based suggestions/results and optional contextual content.

evidence.result: The example uses the list component and adds a leading search icon plus labels; category labels, avatars and chips are optional context additions and are not required for every result set.

checks.statement: Use gaps to separate suggestion or result items into distinct groups.
checks.condition: When the results list contains distinct groups.

sourceHistory.summary: Gaps guidance recommends gaps to separate grouped list items.

implementation.notes: The captured demo has one undivided result list, so the condition of distinct result groups is not present.

checks.statement: Place the search bar where it remains prominent and accessible, typically at the top of the screen; usually keep it at the top of the content and near the content it searches.
checks.condition: When placing a search bar in a screen or view.

sourceHistory.summary: Placement guidance recommends prominent top-of-content placement near searchable content.

evidence.result: The search view is positioned at the top of its bounded scene with a token-backed top inset.

checks.statement: Use docked focused-search results for medium and expanded windows and full-screen results as the default for compact breakpoints; switch between them as window size changes.
checks.condition: When adapting focused search across window sizes.

sourceHistory.summary: Focused layout guidance maps docked and full-screen layouts to breakpoints.

evidence.result: Adaptive search uses the host app width: full-screen below 600px and docked above it. Explicit docked/full-screen configurations remain explicit; changing layout preserves open state and query.
Three tests pass for matching and layout boundaries.
Chromium: ten assertions pass across 390px, 900px and 500px while retaining the query and open state.

fixes.summary: Adapt search results to the host app width without losing input

checks.statement: In contained style, keep the search bar container shape the same when unfocused and focused. Set its margins to 24dp unfocused and 12dp focused. In divided baseline style, separate the bar and results with a divider.
checks.condition: When laying out the search-bar container in either style.

sourceHistory.summary: Container guidance specifies persistent shape, state-dependent margins, and the divided-style divider.

evidence.result: Open and closed states have explicit contained/baseline treatments and margin variables, but the token bindings/actual resolved margins and shape equality were not exercised at runtime.

implementation.notes: Runtime-resolved values for the two margin states remain unobserved.

checks.statement: Use surface container high for the search bar when the background is white or a tonal surface. Avoid placing it on a surface container background; use surface-container roles more than one step apart to preserve contrast.
checks.condition: When choosing the search-bar container color against its screen background.

sourceHistory.summary: Container color guidance specifies backgrounds and warns against adjacent low-contrast surface roles.

evidence.result: Container/background and text colors are token-bound, but source code alone does not prove the specified relative surface step or rendered contrast for every background.

implementation.notes: Resolved color pairs were not measured.

checks.statement: Include either a navigational icon button, such as menu or back, or a non-functional search icon on the leading side.
checks.condition: When a search bar has a leading element.

sourceHistory.summary: Leading icon guidance gives the two acceptable leading-element choices.

evidence.result: The example supports a decorative search leading icon or an accessible menu navigation button; the open-state back button replaces the leading element.

checks.statement: Provide one or two trailing icons or icon buttons for additional search modes, a separate high-level action, overflow, or a decorative search icon. If an avatar is also present, include at most one other trailing icon button. Focused search may show an optional clear icon to remove input text.
checks.condition: When configuring trailing elements on a search bar.

sourceHistory.summary: Trailing icon guidance specifies action examples, count, avatar exception, and optional clear action.

evidence.result: Configured action sets include one/two trailing action combinations and an avatar combination; clear is a separate optional query-dependent action.

checks.statement: Provide short hinted text describing what people can search, such as 'Search replies' or 'Search your messages'.
checks.condition: When a search bar has no entered query.

sourceHistory.summary: Hinted-text guidance recommends a short description of searchable content.

evidence.result: The input has the concise “Search tokens” placeholder and matching accessible name while empty.

checks.statement: Replace hinted text with the entered query when a person starts typing.
checks.condition: When the search field receives query text.

sourceHistory.summary: Input-text guidance specifies that typed query replaces the hint.

evidence.result: The input is a native search field with value bound to the query, so entered text replaces its placeholder.

checks.statement: Keep the search bar close to searchable content and within its pane; scale its width with the layout while anchoring internal elements to the parent's left and right edges.
checks.condition: When the surrounding layout changes size.

sourceHistory.summary: Adaptive-design guidance specifies pane containment, proximity, scaling, and edge anchoring.

evidence.result: Adaptive search width is calculated from its parent layout and margins; the bar and its inner controls remain in the same flex container.

checks.statement: When focused search opens, it may show historical suggestions, suggestions or results while typing, or wait until a query is submitted. Selecting the back icon releases focus, dismisses the list, and restores the original search-bar state.
checks.condition: When focused search is opened or dismissed with the back icon.

sourceHistory.summary: Behavior guidance lists supported suggestion timing and back-icon dismissal behavior.

evidence.result: Back closes the view and restores the collapsed state, but the same close path focuses the search input again; this differs from the source instruction to release focus and needs runtime/focus interpretation.

implementation.notes: The intended focus target after choosing Back is ambiguous against the focus-preserving open/close code.

checks.statement: A search bar may scroll away with content and reappear when the person scrolls up, or remain fixed at the top.
checks.condition: When choosing search-bar scrolling behavior for a screen.

sourceHistory.summary: Scroll guidance describes scrolling-away/reappearing and fixed alternatives.

implementation.notes: The source presents two permitted product scroll policies; this reusable component does not expose a product-level fixed-versus-scroll-away configuration.

checks.statement: Allow a search to execute by typing a query and pressing Enter or by selecting a suggestion/result. Show results in a list below the bar that scrolls beneath it. After a query is submitted, keep the input text visible but unfocused, and show a clear status indicator such as a search icon or Results label.
checks.condition: When executing a search and displaying queried results.

sourceHistory.summary: Search-results guidance specifies execution paths, list placement, query persistence, focus, and a status indicator.

evidence.result: Enter marks the query submitted and focuses a result heading; filtered results stay beneath the bar, and selecting a result opens its content.

checks.statement: On Android, predictive back should detach search from the screen edge to signal that full-screen search will minimize and reveal a preview of the previous screen in the gesture direction.
checks.condition: When implementing predictive back for Android search.

sourceHistory.summary: Predictive-back guidance describes edge detachment and previous-screen preview.

implementation.notes: Predictive-back animation is Android platform integration; this implementation is a web component.

checks.statement: With assistive technology, people must be able to focus the search bar, read its hint or persistent label, enter text and complete a search, interact with suggestions/results, and clear the input.
checks.condition: For accessible search experiences.

sourceHistory.summary: Use cases list the tasks assistive technology users must be able to perform.

evidence.result: The input has a search name and native text entry; the list has named buttons, clear is labeled, and status output is polite live content.

checks.statement: When suggestions or results appear, announce the change to screen-reader users so they know list items are available for selection.
checks.condition: When search suggestions or results become available.

sourceHistory.summary: Autosuggest accessibility guidance requires screen-reader announcement of new results.

evidence.result: Filtering writes suggestion/result availability and count into the search panel live output when suggestions/results are updated.

checks.statement: Place initial focus on the first interactive element, commonly a leading icon button or the text field when there is no leading icon.
checks.condition: When search receives initial focus.

sourceHistory.summary: Initial-focus guidance describes focus placement and the no-leading-icon case.

evidence.result: Resting search presents the leading navigation control before its text field in normal document order. Activating search focuses its text entry; the close control is revealed only for the opened view.

implementation.notes: The previous finding conflated initial navigation into the resting search bar with opening it to type. It does not establish a reason to redirect an explicit search activation to Close.

checks.statement: Support Tab and Shift+Tab to move between interactive elements, Space or Enter to activate the search field for input, and arrow keys to move between result items.
checks.condition: When navigating search by keyboard.

sourceHistory.summary: Keyboard table maps keys to search navigation, activation, and result movement.

evidence.result: Arrow keys move through results and Tab/Shift+Tab cycle controls; Enter submits. The implementation has no explicit Space activation path, while the native search input treats Space as query text, so the source’s Space-to-activate wording needs platform/runtime interpretation.

implementation.notes: The required Space behavior is not mapped to the web textbox semantics.

checks.statement: Use the hinted search text as the search bar's accessibility label. Expose the input as a Text field on Android and a Search field on iOS, and label leading/trailing icon buttons according to icon-button accessibility guidance.
checks.condition: When exposing search controls to assistive technology.
checks.notes: Captured icon-buttons/accessibility guidance says an icon-button label describes the action it performs, such as Add to favorites or Send message.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance specifies search label, platform-specific input role, and icon-button labels.

evidence.result: The web example labels the native type=search input and icon buttons; Android Text field and iOS Search field role mappings are platform-specific and are not implemented by this web specimen.

implementation.notes: Only web semantics were assessed; mobile platform role distinctions are outside this runtime.

checks.statement: Build suggestions and results with the list component so screen readers announce them as a list; follow list accessibility guidance for their labels.
checks.condition: When exposing search suggestions or results to assistive technology.
checks.notes: The captured lists/accessibility guidance says item labels typically combine label and supporting text; selectable list roles and states vary by platform and selection model. Apply the list guidance appropriate to the rendered result list.

sourceHistory.summary: Labeling guidance specifies list semantics and defers item labels to list accessibility guidance.

evidence.result: Suggestions are rendered as a named ul with li rows and list-item buttons, preserving list semantics for screen readers.

checks.statement: Use search to navigate products through queries; use a search app bar as an emphasized global entry point.
checks.condition: When choosing a search entry point for product navigation.

sourceHistory.summary: Overview bullet recommends query-based navigation and a global search app bar.

implementation.notes: Emphasizing global product search versus page-local search is a product navigation decision, not behavior of this reusable search view.

checks.statement: Select the search bar token set for the unfocused bar; use the search view token set for all other search interactions, including styles and layouts.
checks.condition: When selecting token sets for search design or implementation.

sourceHistory.summary: Token section distinguishes unfocused search-bar tokens from all other search-view tokens.

evidence.result: The token generator separately binds md.comp.search-bar to the collapsed bar selector and md.comp.search-view to the focused view selector; interaction tokens are therefore resolved against the view mapping.
